title: Grothendieck's existence theorem for proper schemes over a complete Noetherian ring
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] complete with respect to an ideal $I$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] and $\mathcal I=I\mathcal O_X$. Then the completion functor $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)\to\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$, $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F^\wedge$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], is an equivalence of categories: it is fully faithful, and every object $(\mathcal F_n)$ of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal F^\wedge$ for some coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ [pqf-def-coherent].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Proposition 088C (proposition-existence-proper), Section 0886 (section-existence-proper); its proof uses Lemma 0883 (lemma-fully-faithful), Chow's lemma 0200 (lemma-chow-Noetherian), the projective case Lemma 0885 (lemma-existence-projective), Lemma 088B (lemma-inverse-systems-push-pull) and Lemma 088A (lemma-existence-tricky); EGA III_1 Theorem 5.1.4
